static_traits.name: Lin Kexin
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with colleagues and friends are strained by overwork and perfectionism; has a few friends to communicate with, but finds it hard to truly open up.
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; has not yet received formal psychotherapy related to this problem.
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly organized, able to identify one's own thought patterns; high emotional intensity but guidable; Good cooperativeness, Positive attitude.

basic_info.main_problem: I tend to overwork due to perfectionism, causing stress and tension; recently at Work I spilled soup on my foot, triggering strong negative thoughts, even extreme thoughts of 'want to die'.
basic_info.core_demands: Seeks more effective ways to manage stress and perfectionism, coping with extreme emotional reactions appearing in similar soup-spilling incidents.
growth_experiences: A few years ago, in order to excel professionally, began strengthening perfectionism and overwork, gradually forming the cycle of 'overwork - high stress - making mistakes - extreme emotions', affecting work and daily life.

There has long been a tendency toward perfectionism and overwork, with no formal psychotherapy received yet; Interpersonal relationships affected by work-orientation and high standards, decreased ability to relax and unwind.

core_beliefs: Only by being perfect do I have value
Making a mistake means I am worthless/not good enough

special_situations.event: Accidentally spilling soup on my foot at Work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make a mistake, it means I am incompetent and will be negated
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding any mistakes as much as possible through overwork and setting harsh standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am so stupid, I cannot do anything well, living has no meaning/I want to die

special_situations.event: In busy work phases with many tasks and pressing deadlines
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only doing every item perfectly counts as qualified, otherwise it is failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Overtime, sacrificing rest, persistently pushing oneself in pursuit of zero errors
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I must do everything perfectly, otherwise big problems will occur

special_situations.event: Receiving positive feedback or praise from colleagues
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Unless completely flawless, external affirmation does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring positive feedback and continuing to push harder to prove oneself good enough
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These good reviews do not mean I am really good enough

special_situations.event: Thinking of confiding stress to friends or seeking support
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I express stress, I will trouble others and be seen as weak
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will become a burden to others; better not to say it

core_conflict.wish: Longing to gain a stable sense of worth and recognition through excellence and perfection
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being criticized for imperfection, Being rejected, experiencing shame and loss of control
defense_goal: Avoids mistakes and shame through excessive control and high standards
Turns frustration and anger into self-criticism to maintain a sense of control over evaluation

object_relations.self_representation: A 'not-good-enough person' who may make mistakes at any time and needs to constantly prove their worth
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh, picky judges ready to negate me at any time (superiors/others)

object_relations.self_representation: A person who causes trouble for others
object_relations.object_representation: Others who are easily dragged down by me and thus become annoyed with or distant from me

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about or becoming aware of 'making a mistake' (such as spilling soup) and discussing its impact
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equating mistakes with 'I am not good enough', and anticipating others will negate me for it
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First empathize and name the shame and self-blame, with a gentle tone and slower speech rate; through reflection-clarification distinguish 'mistakes' from 'worth', avoid direct confrontation, and invite them to direct anger at the concrete event rather than the self.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes structured inquiries such as 'finding evidence, reality testing'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing being evaluated/being demanded perfection, worrying my answers are not good enough
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Reducing Interpretation density, turning to present experience; using open-ended questions and gentle pauses, inviting attention to bodily sensations and emotion words.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing the topic of 'asking friends for help / expressing vulnerability'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that expressing will trouble others and be looked down upon
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using an inquiring, non-judgmental tone, employing Socratic Questioning to distinguish 'facts' from 'worries', and encouraging small-step experiments.

manifestations: Equating personal worth with 'perfect without mistakes'; once a mistake occurs, feeling everything is utterly meaningless
Magnifying a single mistake into a total negation of one's existence
outcomes: Increased sense of emptiness and despair

manifestations: Finding it hard to open up to friends, worrying about 'troubling others'
Interpersonal relationships strained by overwork and high standards
outcomes: Stress circulates internally; release channels are limited

manifestations: Bound by the internalized rule 'should achieve perfection'; experiences being controlled by the rule
Lacking a sense of permission for the Freedom of 'existing imperfectly'
outcomes: Narrowed room for choice; guilt and rigidity increase
Worsening Fear of failure and uncertainty

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Repeatedly judges behavior by the self-demand of 'must / should do it perfectly'
Takes external evaluations and performance as the sole basis of worth

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Presumes friends will be 'troubled' by me and colleagues will look down on me, and thus avoids expressing myself
Experiencing dissatisfaction with oneself as others' negation

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-Reflection and self-examination ability, containing excessive self-limitation and self-reproach, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently blaming oneself: 'I am not capable/I do not do well'
Feeling constrained in counseling, worrying one's answers are 'not good enough'

positive_force: Dedicated to work, strong sense of responsibility
Having received positive feedback and objective achievements from colleagues
Able to identify and willing to discuss one's own thought patterns, with clear help-seeking motivation
Has tried time management and self-care, with some initial self-help experience
Has basic social support (several friends to communicate with)
negative_force: Perfectionism and overwork maintaining a high-pressure state
Cognitive biases of black-and-white thinking, catastrophizing, personalization and negating the positive
Binding worth to grades/without mistakes, introjecting the 'must be perfect' rule
Turning to self-blame or even self-injury thoughts when making mistakes, insufficient emotion regulation ability
Avoiding seeking help for fear of troubling others, Insufficient use of social support

antecedent: Facing tasks that require 'doing it perfectly'
target_behavior.core_reason: Binds self-worth to perfect performance, afraid of failure and negative evaluation
target_behavior.function: Avoiding uncertainty and failure feelings, seeking control and recognition
target_behavior.consequence: Work-life imbalance, continuously rising pressure, Interpersonal tension, Difficulty relaxing

target_behavior.behavior: Strong emotional reactions after small mistakes (self-blame, despair, 'want to die' thoughts)
antecedent: Errors occur at work (such as spilling soup on one's feet)
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking, equating one mistake with total failure and worthlessness
target_behavior.function: Briefly easing Anxiety and shame about failure through self-punishment, maintaining a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Emotions fluctuate violently, psychological risk rises, further weakening performance and quality of life

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding expressing stress and seeking help to friends/colleagues
antecedent: When feeling stressed and in need of support
Thinking about discussing troubles with friends
target_behavior.core_reason: Mind-reading presumption that others will be 'troubled' by oneself or look down on oneself
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the possibility of Being rejected or negatively evaluated
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced social support, pressure cycling internally, Relationships growing more distant
